summary: Humboldt County lookout on the Bald Hills ridge in Redwood National and State Parks; built 1940 by the CCC per the register, cab remodeled by CDF, staffed in 2020.

facts.design: L-601 tower; original BC-301 cab replaced by a 732-6A design (remodel plan 962-2A)
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Humboldt-Del Norte Unit (Cal Fire HHU)

access.note: The register calls it an interpretive site for national park visitors. Current hours and whether the cab is open were not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Reached by road up Bald Hills Road; a 2020 visitor walked the final stretch of loose gravel to the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1942 survey describes a wooden structure; the 2020 North Coast Journal account says it was modernized from a wooden original and now has metal walls. Both descriptions can refer to the same lookout at different times.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree: the register gives 1940 (CCC erected the L-601 tower); the North Coast Journal says constructed 1941; the 1942 survey says the lookout was being completed when a 1941 station was occupied. Not resolved. The register's 1976 build date is unexplained; no source read says what happened in 1976. The 1942 'wooden structure' and the register's 'L-601 tower' are reconciled only loosely by the 2020 account of modifications. Current status and access: the register calls it an interpretive site for park visitors, and the 2020 account describes a staffed season, but no source read gives current hours or says whether the cab is open. A search summary described a later trip report calling the lookout closed and gated, and another search summary said the land is Yurok Tribal land; neither was read in a page we could quote, so both are left out and should be checked before publication. The 1965 item is a burglary report, included for history only. No new photos added; the record's register photos are credited to Ron Kemnow, Mark Swift and Fred Johnson, all marked 'All rights reserved'.
